entries.subject: DAMIT 1809: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-1809.txt. Model 1809, version 2017-06-16, pole (180°, 31°), period 7.22439 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 177 ±5 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the documented physical calibration supplies the selected scale. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 173.66 ± 2.65 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 165 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Hanuš et al. (2017), ADAM models
entries.finding: [Hanuš et al. (2017), ADAM models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1702.01996) — retained primary publication; see the body-specific selection and calibration above.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 295, pole ['174', '29'], [Model 295](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/295) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 295: pole (174°, 29°), 7.22439 h, version 2011-02-17, archive diameter 171 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.
